messages:
anita: FYI during the on-prem isolation drill (eu-west rack group) a subset of API nodes started failing decrypts after we tightened egress netpols. KMS 403s observed. 10:52 UTC
raj: Can you confirm if this looks like RBAC (IAM) or network? Any quick logs?
lucy: We rolled the RBAC tightening earlier (removed broad serviceAccount->clusterRoleBinding for 'infra-agent') but that was ~3h before the drill. The timing points to netpol change during the drill though.
frank: Netpol we applied to reduce blast radius (snippet):
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-egress-noninfra
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: workload
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          zone: infra
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```
anita: Audit line from keystore agent (sanitized):
`2026-03-23T10:52:06Z keystore [pod/keystore-7f9] decrypt failed key=projects/_/locations/global/keyRings/rw/cryptoKeys/keystash error=PERMISSION_DENIED: caller does not have permission`
keystore-bot: ALERT keystore-agent/keystore-7f9 returned KMS 403 for decrypt (pod restarts=2)
raj: If the KMS IAM actually lost permission we'd see IAM log entries. Can someone curl the kms endpoint from an affected pod? Also check if egress DNS/NAT to kms.internal.redwood:443 is blocked.
lucy: Ran `kubectl exec` into the pod and did `curl -v https://kms.internal.redwood:443/health` -> connection timed out. From infra nodes it works. Looks like the netpol prevented egress to the internal KMS cluster because the 'zone: infra' label was applied to the wrong set of pods.
anita: Immediate mitigation: add an explicit egress exception for the keystore pods and the metadata/proxy endpoints (kms.internal.redwood + 10.200.0.0/22). We did that and the decrypt errors subsided.
frank: Mitigation commands I ran:
```
kubectl patch networkpolicy deny-egress-noninfra -p '{"spec":{"egress":[{"to":[{"ipBlock":{"cidr":"10.200.0.0/22"}},{"namespaceSelector":{"matchLabels":{"component":"keystore"}}}],"ports":[{"protocol":"TCP","port":443}]}]}}'
kubectl rollout restart deploy/keystore-agent -n infra
```
raj: OK good. For longer-term: we need to preserve least privilege (netpol+RBAC) but avoid fragility. We should add an automated exec test that verifies KMS reachability as part of any netpol change.
lucy: Agreed. Follow-ups I propose: 1) add egress integration test in the netpol CI job that does curl to kms.internal.redwood:443; 2) add a canary tag for netpols to apply to a small set first; 3) document required egress CIDRs/namespaces in the priv-deploy runbook.
anita: I'll open the incident and assign tasks. Quick task split: @lucy revert/adjust netpol exception (done), @frank run canary and validate logs (ongoing), @raj update runbook & add CI test. Also rotate any node-scoped service account tokens affected just in case.
sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-07 created by anita and marked P2. Linked runbook: https://go/infra/incidents/INC-2026-07
frank: Postmortem checklist items I recommend: export keystore audit logs (7d retention currently), confirm no unauthorized IAM changes during the window, add unit test to infra/keystore asserting cached decrypt fallback works if KMS unreachable.
raj: On RBAC side we should avoid removing cloudkms roles from nodes in one sweep. Propose staged IAM policy change with canary tags + a preflight check that verifies nodes can still call KMS before removing roles.
anita: Agreed. Closing interim: the egress exception fixed live traffic; will keep the ticket open for the follow-ups and schedule a 1hr postmortem tomorrow. Action item: add an automated netpol-impact test that runs during CI and run it against staging before any prod netpol change.
sre-bot: Status update INC-2026-07 -> RESOLVED (mitigated) at 11:03 UTC.
anita: Thanks all. Please add any missed items to INC-2026-07 and ping when PRs for the CI check + runbook are up. :thumbsup:
